$comment: Where the vendored copy in this directory came from, and why there is a copy at all.
StandardsEnforcer owns the adapter contract and its schema; this pack owns a declaration
conforming to it. The copy is not a second definition — it is the same bytes, recorded so this
repository's CI can execute the contract it claims to satisfy. Local CI runs in a container with
this repository read-only, no network, and no sibling checkout, so a schema reachable only at
F:/Repos/StandardsEnforcer would make the conformance test unrunnable exactly where it is the
WHAT THE COPY DOES AND DOES NOT ESTABLISH. Validating against it proves standards-adapter.json
conforms to the protocol AS RECORDED AT THE COMMIT BELOW. It cannot prove that commit is still
current — that is a fact about a repository this one cannot see. test/adapter-contract.test.mjs
closes the gap wherever the authoritative checkout is reachable: it compares the bytes and fails
on any difference. Where it is not reachable the freshness check reports itself as unperformed,
and the conformance check still runs. A skipped freshness check is not a passing one.
Do not edit the schema in place. Re-copy it from the authoritative repository and update the
commit below in the same edit, so the recorded provenance and the bytes cannot disagree.
